paper.title: An Unlearning Framework for Continual Learning
paper.one_liner: UnCLe uses a task-embedding-conditioned hypernetwork so tasks can be learned and later unlearned data-free by regressing their generated weights onto Gaussian noise.
paper.summary: Continual learning (CL) trains one model on a stream of tasks and throws away old task data; machine unlearning removes knowledge a model should no longer have. This paper studies a model that receives an arbitrary interleaved sequence of 'learn task t' and 'unlearn task t' requests, where no data of a task is available when it must be unlearned. The authors first adapt six standard unlearning methods (BadTeacher, SCRUB, SalUn, SSD, GKT, JiT) to CL using the DER++ replay buffer and observe two failure modes: unlearning one task damages accuracy on retained tasks (spill), and an unlearned task regains accuracy when later, similar tasks are learned (relapse). UnCLe avoids storing per-task networks: a shared hypernetwork generates a whole task-specific ResNet from a small learned task embedding. Learning a task trains the hypernetwork and a new embedding with a regularizer that keeps the weights generated for old embeddings unchanged. Unlearning trains only the hypernetwork so that the forget-task embedding outputs Gaussian noise (MSE averaged over 10 noise samples), while the same regularizer protects retained tasks; no data is needed. On Permuted-MNIST, 5-Tasks, CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, UnCLe reaches chance-level forget accuracy (about 10%), near-zero spill, low relapse, competitive retain accuracy and MIA of about 50%, and unlearning old tasks frees capacity for new ones.
paper.problem: Existing unlearning algorithms are designed for offline-trained models and mostly need the forget set and/or the retain set, while continual learning discards past-task data. When learn and unlearn requests are interleaved, offline unlearning methods adapted to CL through replay cause unlearning to spill into retained tasks and let unlearned tasks relapse after later learning. Exact solutions based on per-task networks (CLPU) avoid this but cause unbounded parameter growth.
paper.core_idea: Generate task-specific networks with a shared hypernetwork conditioned on per-task embeddings instead of storing them. Each task is then addressed by its embedding, so unlearning a task means retraining the hypernetwork to map that embedding to zero-centred Gaussian noise (a random-like, uninformative network), while a distillation-style output regularizer keeps the weights generated for all other embeddings fixed. This makes unlearning data-free and task-specific, and in experiments the forgotten task does not relapse when new tasks are learned later.
paper.setting: Task-incremental continual learning and unlearning (supervised image classification, centralized): an interleaved sequence of learn/unlearn task requests, past data discarded, task identity known at inference (separate generated network/head per task).
paper.unlearning_type: approximate (data-free, task-level; empirical evaluation only, no certified guarantee)
contributions: Formalizes continual learning and unlearning as a sequence of requests R_i = (I_i, T_i, D_i) with I in {learn, unlearn}, where an unlearn request carries no data (D_i = {}).

Empirical analysis showing that offline unlearning methods (BadTeacher, SCRUB, SalUn, SSD, GKT, JiT) adapted to CL via DER++ replay suffer two failure modes: spill (performance degradation on retained tasks) and relapse (unlearned tasks regaining accuracy after later learning).

UnCLe: a hypernetwork + task-embedding framework where learning uses an output-distillation regularizer and unlearning aligns the forget-task's generated parameters with Gaussian noise, with no data needed and only one small embedding added per task.
Two new metrics for continual unlearning: Spill (unlearning specificity) and Relapse (unlearning permanence), used alongside Retain-task Accuracy and Forget-task Accuracy.
Shows that unlearning obsolete tasks reduces model saturation and improves accuracy on later tasks (e.g., TinyImageNet retained-task accuracy 55.24 vs 50.47 for a learn-only hypernetwork).

Theorem 1 relating the averaged noise-MSE objective to an L2-norm penalty, plus ablations of noising strategies (fixed noise, L2-norm reduction, discarding the embedding) and a burn-in annealing schedule that reduces unlearning time.
method_steps: Set up a fully connected hypernetwork H(.; phi) (hidden layers 128, 256, 512) with Hyperfan initialization so that the generated main-network (ResNet-18/50) weights follow Kaiming-He statistics. The main network is generated in 200 chunks: each 32-dim chunk embedding is concatenated with a 32-dim task embedding, and separate output heads produce conv weights, batch-norm parameters and residual-connection parameters. Chunk embeddings are learned on the first task and then frozen.
On a learn request (L, t, D_t): randomly initialize a new task embedding e_t and freeze a copy of the current hypernetwork parameters phi* = phi.
For each mini-batch of D_t: generate theta_t = H(e_t; phi), compute predictions F(X; theta_t), and compute the task loss L_task (cross-entropy).

Add the regularizer L_reg = (1/(t-1)) * sum_{t'<t} ||H(e_t'; phi*) - H(e_t'; phi)||_2^2 over the stored previous task embeddings (needs no data), weighted by beta; optimize {phi, e_t} on L_task + beta * L_reg with Adam (lr 1e-3). Then store e_t and discard D_t.

On an unlearn request (U, f, no data): for E_u burn-in iterations (100 at first, reduced by 10% after each unlearning operation, minimum 20), sample n = 10 noise vectors z_i ~ N(0, I_d), compute L_fgt = (1/n) * sum_i ||H(e_f; phi) - z_i||_2^2, and update only phi on L_ul = gamma * L_fgt + L_reg, where L_reg keeps the retained tasks' generated parameters fixed (relative to the pre-unlearning hypernetwork).

At inference for a (retained) task t, generate theta_t = H(e_t; phi) and classify with that task-specific network (task-incremental: task identity is given). After unlearning, H(e_f; phi) produces near-zero/noise parameters, so forget-task predictions are near uniform (chance).

key_definitions.name: Request sequence
key_definitions.plain: The model receives an ordered list of requests; each says learn or unlearn a given task, and only learn requests come with data.
key_definitions.formal: R = {R_i}_{i=1}^{|R|}, R_i = (I_i, T_i, D_i); I_i = L => D_i = D_t = {(x_j^t, y_j^t)}; I_i = U => D_i = {} (data-free unlearning)

key_definitions.name: Hypernetwork task-parameter generation
key_definitions.plain: A shared network maps a small task embedding to the full weight vector of that task's classifier.
key_definitions.formal: theta_t = H(e_t; phi); prediction y_hat = F(x; theta_t)

key_definitions.name: Learning objective (Eq. 2)
key_definitions.plain: Fit the new task while keeping the weights generated for all earlier task embeddings unchanged.
key_definitions.formal: argmin_{phi, e_t} L_task(D_t, H(e_t; phi)) + beta * L_reg, L_reg = (1/(t-1)) sum_{t'=1}^{t-1} ||H(e_t'; phi*) - H(e_t'; phi)||_2^2

key_definitions.name: Unlearning objective (Eq. 3)
key_definitions.plain: Push the parameters generated for the forget task toward random Gaussian noise (averaged over n samples so no single noise vector is memorized), while the regularizer protects the other tasks.
key_definitions.formal: argmin_phi gamma * (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n ||H(e_f; phi) - z_i||_2^2 + L_reg, z_i ~ N(0, I_d), n = 10

key_definitions.name: Burn-in (E_u)
key_definitions.plain: Number of optimization iterations spent on one unlearning request; it controls how strongly the task is unlearned.
key_definitions.formal: E_u = 100, annealed by 10% per unlearning operation with floor 20

key_definitions.name: Retain-task Accuracy (RA) / Forget-task Accuracy (FA)
key_definitions.plain: Average accuracy at the end of the sequence over tasks that are still retained / that were unlearned; FA should be near chance (10% for 10-way tasks).
key_definitions.formal: unclear from text beyond 'average accuracy of the retained and the forgotten tasks at the end of the experimental sequence'

key_definitions.name: Spill (Eq. 4)
key_definitions.plain: Total change in accuracy on all non-target tasks caused by one unlearning operation; measures specificity.
key_definitions.formal: S_u = sum_{t != t_f} |a_t^{u-1} - a_t^{u}|, where a_t^{u} is task t's accuracy after operation u

key_definitions.name: Relapse (Eq. 5)
key_definitions.plain: How much a forgotten task's accuracy changes between right after it was unlearned and the end of the sequence; measures permanence.
key_definitions.formal: P_t = |a_t^{u} - a_t^{e}|, u = operation where t was unlearned, e = end of sequence

key_definitions.name: Task relapse
key_definitions.plain: An unlearned task regains accuracy as later (similar) tasks are learned, through backward knowledge transfer, even after its replay data is removed.

key_definitions.name: Unlearning desiderata
key_definitions.plain: Completeness (no remaining trace of the task), specificity (other tasks unaffected) and permanence (cannot come back). Per-task parameter isolation satisfies all three exactly.

key_definitions.name: Uniformity (UNI)
key_definitions.plain: Reported in the ablation table (Table 8) to measure how close forget-task outputs are to a uniform distribution (UnCLe = 100.0, fixed noise = -infinity). Its exact formula is not given in the text.

key_definitions.name: Model saturation
key_definitions.plain: After many tasks a continually trained model loses plasticity and learns new tasks worse; unlearning old tasks restores capacity.

theory.name: Theorem 1 (Appendix E)
theory.statement_plain: For parameters theta in R^d and i.i.d. z_i ~ N(0, I_d), the average (1/n) sum_i ||theta - z_i||^2 converges (almost surely, by the strong law of large numbers) to ||theta||^2 + d as n -> infinity. So averaged noise alignment acts like an L2 penalty that drives the generated parameters toward zero, which makes the forget-task logits zero and its predictions uniform (maximum entropy).
theory.assumptions: theta fixed (not random) and noise samples i.i.d. standard Gaussian; the proof uses E[z_ij] = 0, E[z_ij^2] = 1 and the SLLN.
theory.significance: Explains why noise alignment produces near-uniform forget-task outputs. It also frames n as an interpolation: n = 1 (fixed noise) can be memorized and hurts retained tasks, while n = infinity (pure L2) drives the hypernetwork's own parameters to zero and destabilizes it (Fig. 8). n = 10 is the empirical compromise. Our note (not from the paper): for a single step, (1/n) sum ||theta - z_i||^2 = ||theta - z_bar||^2 + const with z_bar ~ N(0, I/n), so each step regresses onto a fresh random target of variance 1/n.

theory.name: Informal argument: parameter isolation gives exact unlearning (Methodology)
theory.statement_plain: If every task has its own separate model, deleting that model is exact unlearning: it is complete (no other network holds the task), specific (other networks are untouched) and permanent (nothing can be recovered from the rest).
theory.assumptions: Disjoint parameters per task and no shared components.
theory.significance: Gives the ideal UnCLe approximates: it keeps the task-addressable modularity through embeddings and avoids parameter growth by sharing a hypernetwork. The price is that unlearning is only approximate.

paper.complexity: No formal complexity analysis. Storage: one hypernetwork plus a 32-dim embedding per task (200 frozen 32-dim chunk embeddings), described as negligible growth, versus one full network per task for CLPU. Learning: each step generates a full ResNet in 200 chunks and evaluates L_reg over all previous task embeddings with both phi and frozen phi*, so the cost grows linearly with the number of past tasks. Unlearning: E_u burn-in iterations (100, annealed 10% per op, min 20) of hypernetwork-only optimization. No data and no main-network forward passes are needed, so the cost does not depend on dataset size. Measured average unlearning time on one V100 (Table 10): 33.28 s (5-Tasks), 13.16 s (Permuted-MNIST), 41.70 s (CIFAR-100), 29.63 s (TinyImageNet). SalUn takes 491.9/358.3/51.47/65.20 s and SCRUB 171.1/118.9/30.02/32.52 s, but SSD (5.73 s CIFAR-100, 5.81 s TinyImageNet) and BadTeacher (10.95/8.68 s) are faster on the larger datasets. Annealing cut TinyImageNet unlearning time from 45.12 to 29.63 s and CIFAR-100 from 43.98 to 41.70 s at the same FA of 10.00 (Table 7).

datasets: 5-Tasks / Five-datasets: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, notMNIST, SVHN (5 tasks x 10 classes; 7-request sequences)
TinyImageNet (200 classes; the analysis section and Table 4 sequences use 20 tasks x 10 classes, while the Datasets paragraph says 10 tasks; 30-request sequences)
models: Hypernetwork: fully connected MLP with hidden layers 128/256/512, task and chunk embedding dim 32, 200 chunks, separate heads for weights/BN/residual parameters, Hyperfan init
Main network: ResNet-18 (Permuted-MNIST main results; all datasets in appendix)
Main network: ResNet-50 (5-Tasks, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet main results)
baselines: Offline unlearning methods adapted to CL with DER++ replay: BadTeacher, SCRUB, SalUn, SSD (all need forget + retain data), JiT (forget data only), GKT (data-free)
UniCLUN (BadTeacher + replay for CL; treated as equivalent to the BadTeacher adaptation and not reported separately)
CLPU (separate network per task, exact unlearning by deletion)
Hypernetwork-based ablations: JiT-Hnet, GKT-Hnet, Hnet (unlearning only through natural catastrophic forgetting)
Oracle-style baselines with full retain-task data: FT* (fine-tune on retain set), RT* (retrain from scratch), RT-Hnet* (retrain a hypernetwork sequentially)
Noising-strategy ablations: Fixed-noise alignment (n=1), L2-norm reduction (n=inf), Discard e_f (replace embedding with random)
metrics: Per-task accuracy trajectories over request sequences
headline_results: Table 1 (Seq. 1, 3 seeds) RA/FA: Permuted-MNIST UnCLe 96.87/10.00 vs BadTeacher 92.17/10.20, SalUn 92.39/59.24, CLPU 91.73/-; CIFAR-100 UnCLe 62.65/10.00 vs SalUn 66.56/44.89, JiT 65.94/43.93, BadTeacher 61.75/14.57; 5-Tasks UnCLe 94.12/10.04 vs CLPU 85.00, SalUn 74.75/25.02, BadTeacher 54.38/8.55; TinyImageNet UnCLe 55.24/10.00 vs SalUn 58.44/36.02, JiT 57.86/32.70, BadTeacher 52.79/15.73.
Table 2 Spill (lower is better): UnCLe 0.044 (PMNIST), 0.640 (CIFAR-100), 0.023 (5-Tasks), 0.722 (TinyImageNet) vs baselines roughly 5-83 (e.g., GKT 51.86/32.96/83.08/16.36).

Table 2 Relapse: UnCLe 8.703 (PMNIST), 0.507 (CIFAR-100, lowest), 0.539 (5-Tasks, 2nd after SCRUB 0.00), 2.233 (TinyImageNet; SCRUB 0.739 lower). SCRUB has low relapse but collapses RA (e.g., 9.97 on PMNIST). BadTeacher relapse is 30.51 (PMNIST) and 23.57 (CIFAR-100).

MIA: UnCLe 50.00 +/- 0.00-0.02 on PMNIST, CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet (50.01 on 5-Tasks). Most baselines are also about 45-53% because task-incremental forget heads are randomized, so MIA does not discriminate much in this setting.
Saturation (Table 3): retained-task accuracy for UnCLe vs Only-Learning hypernetwork is 55.24 vs 50.47 (TinyImageNet), 62.65 vs 60.51 (CIFAR-100), 96.87 vs 96.84 (PMNIST), 94.12 vs 94.12 (5-Tasks).

Noising ablation (Table 8): Fixed noise lowers RA (CIFAR-100 21.79, 5-Tasks 83.04); Norm reduction keeps RA but forgets poorly (FA 94.99 PMNIST, 34.42 CIFAR-100); Discard e_f leaves FA high (61.79 PMNIST); UnCLe FA 10.00 with UNI 100.0.

Appendix: the Hnet baseline that relies on natural forgetting keeps forget-task accuracy high (FA 96.91 PMNIST, 54.31 TinyImageNet), so hypernetworks barely forget on their own. FT* with full retain data still has FA 67.70 (PMNIST) and 55.44 (CIFAR-100).

limitations: Stated: works only at task granularity; cannot learn or unlearn individual classes within a task (no class-incremental learning/unlearning).
Assumes task-incremental CL with known task identity at inference and a separate generated network per task, which makes forgetting easier to realize and MIA uninformative (all methods about 50%).

No formal unlearning guarantee: forgetting is judged by FA near chance, spill, relapse and MIA. Information about the forgotten task may persist in the shared hypernetwork weights phi (e.g., relearn-speed attacks are not tested).

Relapse is not uniformly the lowest (SCRUB is lower on PMNIST, 5-Tasks and TinyImageNet; UnCLe relapse is 8.70 on PMNIST). RA is below SalUn/JiT on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet and below the FT* oracle.

Unlearning time is not the lowest on larger datasets (SSD, BadTeacher and JiT are faster on CIFAR-100/TinyImageNet), and the learning-time regularizer cost grows with the number of stored task embeddings.
Short request sequences (7-30), vision classification only, 3 seeds, and per-dataset tuning of beta and gamma using FA/RA (the selection criterion uses the evaluation metrics).

Internal inconsistencies in the text: TinyImageNet described as both 10 and 20 tasks; unlearning described both as reverting to standard-normal/Kaiming initialization and as driving parameters to zero; gamma called a 'regularization' strength but multiplies the forget term; UNI metric is undefined; some table references are broken ('??'). It is unclear whether the forgotten task's embedding is deleted or kept in L_reg after unlearning.
future_work: Extend to class-incremental learning and unlearning, i.e., learning and unlearning individual classes within tasks (stated).
Develop robust verification mechanisms and unlearning algorithms that guard against relapse of supposedly forgotten information (stated in Broader Impact).
paper.relevance_to_efficient_unlearning: UnCLe shows a cheap, data-free way to unlearn: if knowledge is addressable by a small key (a task embedding feeding a hypernetwork), unlearning becomes a short optimization over the generator (100 or fewer iterations, no data passes, cost independent of dataset size) rather than retraining. It also gives an efficient-unlearning project two evaluation tools, Spill and Relapse, which expose failure modes that RA/FA miss and are relevant whenever unlearning is followed by more training. The noising-strategy ablation and Theorem 1 are a useful worked example of how the choice of 'unlearning target' (fixed noise vs averaged noise vs zero) trades off forgetting quality against damage to retained knowledge. As a pitfall, it shows that offline methods (SalUn, JiT, BadTeacher) look fine at one time step but relapse later. It also sits between exact isolation (SISA/CLPU-style, expensive in storage) and shared-parameter approximate unlearning, which is the main design axis for efficient unlearning.
open_questions: Class- or sample-level unlearning inside a hypernetwork framework, and class-incremental (no task-ID) settings where generated heads are shared.
Can noise-alignment unlearning be given a formal guarantee, e.g., bounding the distance between the post-unlearning hypernetwork and one never trained on task f, or a certified/DP-style bound?
How robust is UnCLe to relearning attacks (fine-tuning on a few forget-task samples) compared with a retrained-from-scratch hypernetwork, i.e., does knowledge persist in shared phi?
Reduce the O(#tasks) cost of the output regularizer (e.g., sampling a subset of stored embeddings per step) and analyse when it fails to protect retained tasks.
Combine hypernetwork-based data-free unlearning with federated continual learning (clients generating task heads), where per-client task removal must be cheap in communication.
Explain theoretically why averaged noise (n=10) beats both fixed noise and pure L2 shrinkage, and whether an adaptive n or target distribution gives better retain/forget trade-offs.

nodes.label: Machine Unlearning
nodes.description: Removing the influence of specific training data, classes or tasks from a trained model so it behaves as if never trained on them, ideally without full retraining.

nodes.label: Continual Learning
nodes.description: Training a model on a sequence of tasks arriving over time, typically without retaining past data, while avoiding forgetting of earlier tasks and enabling knowledge transfer.

nodes.label: Continual Learning and Unlearning
nodes.description: Setting where a model receives interleaved learning and unlearning requests over time and must acquire new knowledge and remove specific past knowledge without disrupting the rest.

nodes.label: Approximate Unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning that updates a model to approximately mimic one retrained without the forgotten data, with empirical rather than exact equivalence.

nodes.label: Exact Unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning whose output is identical (in distribution) to retraining from scratch without the deleted data.

nodes.label: Data-free Unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning carried out without access to the forget set or retain set, relying only on the model (and possibly synthetic signals).

nodes.label: Right to be Forgotten
nodes.description: Legal right (e.g., GDPR Art. 17) for individuals to have their personal data erased, which motivates removing data influence from trained models.

nodes.label: Data Privacy
nodes.description: Protection of personal or sensitive information from disclosure or misuse, including leakage through trained models.

nodes.label: Task-Incremental Learning
nodes.description: Continual learning scenario in which each task has its own output space or head and the task identity is available at test time.

nodes.label: Class-Incremental Learning
nodes.description: Continual learning scenario in which new classes arrive over time and the model must discriminate among all seen classes without task identity at test time.

nodes.label: Knowledge Distillation
nodes.description: Training a model to match the outputs (or parameters) of another model; in continual learning it keeps a new model close to an old one on past tasks.

nodes.label: UnCLe
nodes.description: Unlearning framework for continual learning in which a hypernetwork generates task-specific networks from task embeddings, and a task is unlearned without data by aligning its generated parameters with Gaussian noise.

nodes.label: Hypernetwork
nodes.description: A neural network that outputs the weights of another (main/target) network, usually conditioned on an input embedding.

nodes.label: Continual Learning with Hypernetworks
nodes.description: Continual learning approach (von Oswald et al., 2020) in which a hypernetwork produces task-specific weights from task embeddings and an output regularizer keeps previously generated weights fixed.

nodes.label: Task Embedding
nodes.description: A learned low-dimensional vector identifying a task, used to condition a shared model such as a hypernetwork to produce task-specific behaviour.

nodes.label: Chunked Hypernetwork
nodes.description: Hypernetwork that produces the main network's parameters in chunks by conditioning on learned chunk embeddings, which keeps the output layer small for large target networks.

nodes.label: Hypernetwork Output Regularizer
nodes.description: Regularizer penalizing the squared difference between the weights a hypernetwork currently generates for stored task embeddings and those generated by a frozen earlier copy, preventing forgetting without stored data.

nodes.label: Noise-Alignment Unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning a task by training a weight generator so that the parameters it produces for that task match freshly sampled zero-mean Gaussian noise, with the MSE averaged over several samples.

nodes.label: Burn-in Annealing
nodes.description: Schedule that reduces the number of unlearning optimization iterations (burn-in) by a fixed fraction after each unlearning operation, down to a minimum.

nodes.label: Hyperfan Initialization
nodes.description: Initialization scheme for hypernetworks chosen so that the generated main-network weights have the variance of standard initializations such as Kaiming He.

nodes.label: Parameter Isolation
nodes.description: Continual learning strategy that assigns disjoint parameters (separate networks or sub-networks) to each task so tasks cannot interfere.

nodes.label: DER++
nodes.description: Dark Experience Replay++: replay-based continual learning that stores past inputs, labels and logits and trains with classification loss plus logit matching on buffer samples.

nodes.label: Experience Replay
nodes.description: Continual learning technique that stores a small buffer of past examples and replays them while training on new tasks to reduce forgetting.

nodes.label: BadTeacher
nodes.description: Unlearning method that distils from a competent teacher on retain data and from an incompetent (randomly initialized) teacher on forget data using KL divergence.

nodes.label: SCRUB
nodes.description: Student-teacher unlearning method in which the student is trained to move away from the teacher on forget data while staying close to it on retain data.

nodes.label: SalUn
nodes.description: Saliency-based unlearning that builds a gradient-based weight saliency map for the forget set and updates only the salient weights.

nodes.label: SSD
nodes.description: Selective Synaptic Dampening: retraining-free unlearning that uses Fisher information to find parameters important to the forget set and dampens them.

nodes.label: GKT
nodes.description: Zero-shot unlearning method that uses a generator to synthesize pseudo-samples and gated knowledge transfer to remove forget-class knowledge without real data.

nodes.label: JiT
nodes.description: Zero-shot unlearning method that uses Lipschitz continuity, smoothing the model's outputs with respect to perturbations of forget samples.

nodes.label: CLPU
nodes.description: Continual Learning and Private Unlearning: learns a separate network for each task that may need forgetting and deletes it on request, giving exact unlearning.

nodes.label: UniCLUN
nodes.description: Unified continual learning and unlearning framework that adapts BadTeacher-style random-teacher distillation to a continual setting with a replay buffer.

nodes.label: Retrain from Scratch
nodes.description: Naive exact unlearning that retrains a model from initialization on the remaining data.

nodes.label: Fine-tuning Unlearning
nodes.description: Approximate unlearning baseline that fine-tunes the trained model on the retain set only, relying on forgetting of the removed data.

nodes.label: Fixed-Noise Alignment
nodes.description: Unlearning variant that regresses a task's generated parameters onto a single fixed noise sample (n = 1).

nodes.label: L2-Norm Reduction Unlearning
nodes.description: Unlearning variant that minimizes the L2 norm of a task's generated parameters, pushing them to zero; the n -> infinity limit of noise alignment.

nodes.label: Discard Task Embedding
nodes.description: Trivial unlearning variant that replaces the forget task's embedding with a random one without retraining the generator.

nodes.label: Catastrophic Forgetting
nodes.description: Abrupt loss of performance on previously learned tasks when a neural network is trained on new data.

nodes.label: Task Relapse
nodes.description: Phenomenon where a previously unlearned task regains performance after the model learns other, often similar, tasks.

nodes.label: Unlearning Spill
nodes.description: Collateral damage in which unlearning one target degrades performance on other retained tasks or data, i.e. a lack of specificity.

nodes.label: Utility Degradation
nodes.description: Loss of model accuracy or usefulness on retained data caused by an unlearning procedure.

nodes.label: Model Saturation
nodes.description: Loss of plasticity in a continually trained model as it accumulates tasks, reducing its ability to learn new ones.

nodes.label: Stability-Plasticity Trade-off
nodes.description: Tension between preserving old knowledge (stability) and acquiring new knowledge (plasticity) in continual learning.

nodes.label: Membership Inference Attack
nodes.description: Attack that infers whether a given example was part of a model's training set from the model's behaviour.

nodes.label: Backward Transfer
nodes.description: Effect that learning a new task has on performance on earlier tasks; positive backward transfer improves old tasks.

nodes.label: Parameter Growth
nodes.description: Growth in model size as tasks are added, e.g. when each task receives its own network, which violates memory limits in continual learning.

nodes.label: Unlearning Cost
nodes.description: Computational time, memory and data needed to process an unlearning request.

nodes.label: Noise-MSE to L2 Theorem
nodes.description: Result that the average squared distance between a fixed parameter vector and n i.i.d. standard Gaussian samples converges almost surely to its squared L2 norm plus the dimension as n grows.

nodes.label: Completeness, Specificity, Permanence
nodes.description: Desired properties of unlearning: completeness (no trace of forgotten knowledge), specificity (no effect on other knowledge) and permanence (forgotten knowledge does not return).

nodes.label: Retain Accuracy
nodes.description: Accuracy on the data, classes or tasks that should be kept after unlearning.

nodes.label: Forget Accuracy
nodes.description: Accuracy on the data, classes or tasks that were supposed to be unlearned; ideally at chance level or equal to a retrained model.

nodes.label: Spill
nodes.description: Sum of absolute accuracy changes on all non-target tasks caused by a single unlearning operation; measures unlearning specificity.

nodes.label: Relapse
nodes.description: Absolute change in a forgotten task's accuracy between right after it was unlearned and a later point; measures unlearning permanence.

nodes.label: Unlearning Time
nodes.description: Wall-clock time required to process an unlearning request.

nodes.label: MIA Success Rate
nodes.description: Accuracy of a membership inference attacker; 50% means the attacker does no better than random guessing.

nodes.label: Uniformity (UNI)
nodes.description: Score of how close a model's predictive distribution on forgotten inputs is to uniform (maximum entropy).

nodes.label: Permuted-MNIST
nodes.description: Continual learning benchmark in which each task applies a fixed random pixel permutation to MNIST images.

nodes.label: 5-Tasks (Five-datasets)
nodes.description: Continual learning benchmark of five 10-class datasets learned as separate tasks: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, notMNIST and SVHN.

nodes.label: MNIST
nodes.description: Dataset of 70k 28x28 grayscale handwritten digit images in 10 classes.

nodes.label: Fashion-MNIST
nodes.description: Dataset of 70k 28x28 grayscale clothing images in 10 classes, a drop-in replacement for MNIST.

nodes.label: SVHN
nodes.description: Street View House Numbers: real-world colour digit images in 10 classes.

nodes.label: CIFAR-100
nodes.description: Dataset of 60k 32x32 colour images in 100 classes.

nodes.label: Tiny ImageNet
nodes.description: Subset of ImageNet with 200 classes of 64x64 images.

nodes.label: ResNet-18
nodes.description: 18-layer residual convolutional neural network.

nodes.label: ResNet-50
nodes.description: 50-layer residual convolutional neural network with bottleneck blocks.

edges.note: Proposes UnCLe as a unified, data-free framework for continual learning and unlearning.

cross_paper.note: Both target joint continual learning and unlearning. UnCLe generates full task networks with a hypernetwork and unlearns by noise alignment, whereas BID-LoRA uses parameter-efficient LoRA modules. UnCLe's Spill/Relapse metrics and baselines are natural comparison points.

UnCLe argues that isolating parameters (as in SISA-style sharding or CLPU per-task models) gives exact unlearning but grows storage. It instead shares one hypernetwork and accepts approximate, data-free unlearning. SISA is not cited.

MeCo addresses knowledge-efficient federated continual learning without an unlearning operation. UnCLe's embedding-addressable, data-free task unlearning is a candidate mechanism for adding unlearning to such FCL systems.

FedShard pursues efficient federated unlearning via sharded retraining, which is exact-style and data-dependent. UnCLe performs centralized, data-free approximate task unlearning by editing a hypernetwork.
